title: What are all the other angles inside these two rectangles?
description: Two rectangles have their diagonals drawn, and one angle is given in each. The video uses the equal halves of the diagonals to see isosceles triangles, finds every other angle, and checks the angles of a triangle at the end.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other in half, so each triangle at the crossing has two equal sides and two equal angles. Watch for students who halve the angle at the crossing instead of sharing what is left of one hundred eighty.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 1)
video_script.why: The child uses the equal diagonals of a rectangle, which cut each other in half, to find equal angles in the triangles at the crossing and then every other angle.
video_script.substitution: Use the equal halves of the diagonals to see the isosceles triangles, take the angle sum of a triangle, and use the right angle at each corner and the straight line at O.
video_script.anchor: rectangle ABCD and rectangle PQRS with their diagonals crossing at O
video_script.payoff_line: Every angle in both rectangles is now found

final_answer.spoken: every angle in both rectangles is now found

hold_back: every angle in both rectangles is found
maths_rules: the diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other in half, so OA = OB = OC = OD
rectangle ABCD, angle CAB = 30 degrees: OA = OB, so angle ABD = 30 degrees
angle CAD = 90 - 30 = 60 degrees; OA = OD, so angle ADB = 60 degrees
angle BDC = 30, angle ACD = 30, angle ACB = 60 degrees
triangle OAB: angle AOB = 180 - 30 - 30 = 120 degrees; angle AOD = 180 - 120 = 60 degrees
rectangle PQRS, angle QOR = 110 degrees: angle POS = 110 (vertically opposite); angle QOP = angle ROS = 180 - 110 = 70 degrees
triangle QOR: OQ = OR, base angles add to 180 - 110 = 70, so each is 35 degrees
angle OQP = 90 - 35 = 55 degrees; in the same way angle OPQ = angle ORS = angle OSR = 55 and angle OPS = angle OSP = 35 degrees
video_script.design: One idea: equal halves of the diagonals make isosceles triangles at the crossing. The two rectangles with their diagonals stay on the board throughout.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>Here is a question from your book about two rectangles.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Take rectangle eigh B C D, with its diagonals meeting at O.
<bookmark mark='ang'/>Angle C eigh B is thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='second'/>In rectangle P Q R S, angle Q O R is one hundred ten degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can we find every other angle inside both rectangles?

narration: <bookmark mark='equal'/>The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other in half.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>That makes O the same distance from all four corners. Every triangle at O then has two equal sides.

narration: <bookmark mark='equal'/>Step one, in rectangle eigh B C D, O eigh equals O B.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Triangle O eigh B has two equal angles, and angle eigh B D is thirty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: ∠CAD = 90° − 30° = 60°; OA = OD, so ∠ADB = 60°; in the same way ∠BDC = 30°, ∠ACD = 30°, ∠ACB = 60°

marks.od: triangle OAD is shaded and its base angles glow at 60°

beats.colours: triangle OAD in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='corner'/>Step two, the corner at eigh is ninety degrees. Angle C eigh D is ninety minus thirty, which is sixty.
<bookmark mark='od'/>O eigh equals O D, so angle eigh D B is also sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>In the same way, angles B D C and eigh C D are thirty. Angle eigh C B is sixty.

marks.sum: the three angles of triangle OAB are written with a total of 180°
marks.line: angles AOB and AOD sit on a straight line through O

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step three, the angles of triangle O eigh B add to one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Take away thirty and thirty, and angle eigh O B is one hundred twenty. Angle eigh O D shares a straight line with it, so it is sixty.

marks.opp: angles P O S and Q O R glow as the pair across the crossing
marks.line: angle Q O P sits on a straight line with angle Q O R

beats.colours: the crossing angles in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='opp'/>Step four, take rectangle P Q R S. Angle P O S is across from angle Q O R, so it is one hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Angle Q O P makes a straight line with angle Q O R, so it is seventy. Angle R O S is seventy too.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: in △QOR, OQ = OR and the base angles add to 180° − 110° = 70°, so each is 35°; ∠OQP = 90° − 35° = 55°; the others follow: 55°, 55°, 35°, 35°

marks.base: the base angles of triangle QOR glow and share 70°
marks.half: each base angle is written as 35°
marks.corner: the right angle at Q splits into 35° and 55°
marks.rest: the matching angles at P, R and S are written beside the figure

narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>Step five, triangle Q O R has two equal sides. Its base angles share one hundred eighty minus one hundred ten, which is seventy.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Each base angle is thirty five.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>Angle O Q P is ninety minus thirty five, which is fifty five.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other corners work the same way, giving fifty five, fifty five, thirty five and thirty five.

marks.back: the three angles of triangle QOP are written and added to 180°

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step six, put the answers back. In triangle Q O P, seventy, fifty five and fifty five add to one hundred eighty.

beats.on_screen: Answer: every angle in both rectangles is found. First rectangle: 30°, 60°, 120°. Second rectangle: 110°, 70°, 35°, 55°

marks.list: the angles of each rectangle are listed beside its figure

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every angle in both rectangles is now found.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The first has thirty, sixty and one hundred twenty. The second has one hundred ten, seventy, thirty five and fifty five.
